articles.title: Borrowed References, Local Languages: Blended Styles on Latin American Façades
articles.summary: Architectural styles are often identified through a familiar set of characteristics: particular forms, materials, proportions, and decorative elements. Yet these characteristics do not always remain tied to the traditions from which they originate. A classical column may appear on a self-built house , a modernist ceramic composition may be reproduced across a residential façade, or a chalet may become part of a multistory commercial building . Each retains something recognizable from its precedent , although its application reflects a different set of architectural decisions.

articles.title: Shenzhen UDC Multifunctional Space / of gaaarden design
articles.summary: Traditionally, offices, retail spaces, and places for social activities have had clear boundaries. As lifestyles change, however, we are seeing these boundaries gradually become less distinct. Located in a high-rise office building in Qianhai, Shenzhen , UDC is a multifunctional space that brings together fashion retail, work, social activities, and brand events. Through this project, we explored how to move beyond the fixed boundaries between different activities, allowing them to connect and overlap within the same space to create new spatial experiences.

articles.title: S House / BOV ESTUDIO / BOV ESTUDIO
articles.summary: In Ayllón (Segovia), adjacent to the historic center, the openings of a 1910 facade now look out onto a courtyard. The facade originally belonged to a family home that was divided into two dwellings in the mid-1940s. Decades later, the owner reunited one of those halves with two adjacent plots to build his primary residence. He wanted a house that could be navigated without steps, and where proximity to the street was compatible with family privacy.

articles.title: Fig Tree House / Estúdio Lava

The semicircular shape stems from the intention to orient the building towards both the sunset and the open sea horizon across the island of Gipóia.

articles.title: Espira Yoga Shala / Arquitectura Mixta
articles.summary: Inspired by the delicate wings of Costa Rica's glasswing butterfly, Espira explores the relationship between lightness, balance, and suspended movement through a sculptural bamboo structure. Located within the Peninsula Papagayo Sports Complex in Guanacaste, Costa Rica, the Yoga Shala translates these natural qualities into an open architectural form designed to encourage stillness, awareness, and a deeper connection with the surrounding landscape.
